subject.title: docs(durable): propose durable core runtime boundary and validation plan

question: Should this durable core runtime RFC replace or fold into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98717, or should it remain a separate five-part durable-core stack?
rationale: The patch is docs-only, but accepting it would publish a core runtime architecture direction that overlaps an existing open durable-runtime RFC and companion implementation stack.

options.title: Use the existing RFC as canonical
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98717 as the canonical durable-runtime RFC and fold only useful validation-plan text from this branch into that path after docs metadata is fixed.

options.title: Switch to this stack
options.body: If maintainers prefer the newer durable-core split, require the author to repair docs metadata and explain how the older RFC and follow-up PRs should be retargeted or closed.

options.title: Pause durable runtime direction
options.body: If the core boundary is not accepted yet, pause or close the RFC stack until maintainers sponsor a concrete architecture direction.

recommendation.title: Use the existing RFC as canonical
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98717 as the canonical durable-runtime RFC and fold only useful validation-plan text from this branch into that path after docs metadata is fixed.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is a core architecture and public-docs direction choice, and Peter is both the project decision lead and the visible current specs/docs-map history owner.
